revealed.theme: the marks a life leaves on a room — and who is allowed to leave them. Renting is the stated hour, but the thread that keeps pulling is dad's workshop: the groove, the pencil lines, the space that turned out to be 'only ever a room'.

collisions.connection: Both invert who the suspect is. 'protected from who...they mean protected from me' and 'photographing scuffs I didn't make so I can prove I didn't make them' — in both the tenant is treated as the threat to their own home, defending themselves against an accusation nobody has made yet.
collisions.question: When did living somewhere start meaning building a legal case that you were ever there at all?
collisions.extension: An hour of proving negatives about a hallway, then a lifetime of proving you didn't wear the groove into the floor.

collisions.connection: Both measure a thing by the ceremony it doesn't get. Forty years of dad 'empty by the Monday'; the 'biggest thing I spend money on' leaving as 'a standing order in the dark'. The magnitude and the ritual are wildly mismatched in each.
collisions.question: What would a rite look like for the two transactions that actually move a life — clearing out and paying to stay?
collisions.extension: The standing order goes out in the dark the same way the lock-up emptied over a weekend: the big things happen with no one watching and no bell rung.

collisions.connection: Both strip the mythology off a space to leave the plain fact. 'characterful just means broken but old' and 'turns out it was only ever a room' — the agent's word and the son's grief doing the same demolition, one cynical, one accidental.
collisions.question: Is 'characterful' the lie you resent, or the one you wanted someone to tell about dad's lock-up?
collisions.extension: Someone's rowing machine where the workbench stood — characterful, the agent would call it. Broken but old. The only word they own.

eureka.why_now: Today's renewal email — 'evidence that I live there is a chargeable offence' — lands on a month of dad's traces (the pencil lines, the worn groove, the lock-up that's 'only ever a room') and names exactly what renting forbids: the marks that made his space his.
eureka.question: Dad wore a groove into the bench by leaning thirty years in one spot — what's the tenant's version of that groove, and what does it cost per year?
eureka.extension: He never measured twice, just marked the wood. A whole year somewhere where the marking itself — the blu-tack, the leaning, the living — is the damage you pay for.
